title: NZ NCSC: 1,694 incident reports in Q3 2026, busiest quarter in two years
date_note: NCSC and SecurityBrief pages are dated 25 November (New Zealand time); no earlier day is given, and 25 November NZ time is still 24 November UTC.
geo_basis: Agency headquarters city; the report covers New Zealand
summary: New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre says it recorded 1,694 cyber security incident reports in the third quarter of 2026, up from 1,129 in the previous quarter. SecurityBrief New Zealand reports that reported direct financial losses rose to $5.9 million from $2.7 million. The NCSC describes it as its busiest quarter in two years.
plain: New Zealand's cyber agency received 1,694 incident reports in July to September 2026, up from 1,129 the quarter before, and reported direct financial losses rose to $5.9 million from $2.7 million.
exec: NZ's NCSC logged 1,694 incident reports in Q3 2026, up from 1,129, with reported direct losses of $5.9 million.
action: NCSC New Zealand advises reviewing cyber security settings, making sure basic protections are in place and staying vigilant against sophisticated online threats.

key_findings: The NCSC received 1,694 incident reports in the third quarter of 2026, up from 1,129 in the second quarter, its highest quarterly total in about two years.
Direct financial losses reported to the NCSC reached $5.9 million, up from $2.7 million in the second quarter.
Phishing and credential harvesting was the most common category, with scams and fraud second.
The NCSC says reported incidents rose in every category and attributes part of the rising risk to frontier AI systems that can speed up finding and exploiting vulnerabilities.
recommendations: Make sure basic protections are in place.
Stay vigilant against increasingly sophisticated online threats.
